playbook:
When I calculate the per-token return, I check whether contributing pays for me: if the multiplier divided by the group size is below 1, each token contributed costs more than it returns, so free-riding is my dominant strategy and I contribute 0 regardless of what others do.

In any similar sealed-contribution game, before round 1 I compute: return per contributed token = multiplier / players. Below 1 → always 0, above 1 → always max, exactly 1 → indifferent so keep tokens for certainty. In this game (1.6 / 4 = 0.4) every contributed token returns only 0.4, so the answer was locked in before the game started.

When receipts must exactly match envelope contents and are checked by a referee, I never consider deception — I always declare the true amount, since any mismatch costs me. I don't over-explain the receipt line; the truthful bracketed token is all that's needed.

When I'm deciding my contribution, I ignore the temptation to "be nice" or restart cooperation unilaterally; contributing only pays if I have a concrete reason to believe others will match me AND the return math favors me — both conditions, not one. Here others matching me still wouldn't help, because 0.4 per token loses money even at full cooperation; so even a cooperative group is no reason to contribute.

When I'm ahead on score, I protect the lead: contributing 0 keeps my full endowment, and since the share is split equally, contributing can never gain me relative ground against players who contribute less or the same. Conversely, when I'm behind in a below-1 game, contributing still doesn't help me catch up unless the leader contributes more than me — the same math that makes it lose makes expecting others to bankroll my comeback unreliable.

When everyone else stops contributing, I treat the cooperative phase as over and do not try to revive it alone — a lone contribution just donates 60% of my tokens to the others. Round 2's all-zero round confirmed the collapse instantly, and I read each round's published receipts to confirm nothing has changed before repeating 0.

When it's early and I want information, I can contribute 0 anyway in a game with published receipts, because others' play is revealed for free; I don't need to spend tokens to learn. This paid off in round 1: I learned all three opponents contributed 20 while banking 44 total.

I watch for the risk that others' cooperative play could erase my lead: in round 1 the others' full contributions only earned them 24 while I earned 44, so their generosity widened my gap. In a below-1 game I don't fear others cooperating — it pays me more than them.

When the multiplier-to-players ratio ever exceeds 1 (the share I get back per token exceeds the token's value), I flip: full contribution becomes dominant and I contribute the maximum every round, since then even my own unilateral contribution profits me.

When a win is already mathematically locked before the last round, I still contribute 0 to bank the full endowment rather than padding a tied pot. In the final round in particular there is no future to invest in, so 0 is doubly correct.

I keep replies short: one line of return math and the bracketed token. No elaborate justification is needed once the dominant strategy is identified.

PUBLIC GOODS -- you, Ines, Jo and Kit; 5 rounds; a fresh endowment of 20 tokens each round.
Each round every player seals a contribution of 0 to 20 tokens in an envelope, then files a receipt slip stating the amount. A receipt must state the envelope's exact amount. Envelopes go to the vault; the receipts are published.
The pot -- the receipts total -- is multiplied by 1.6 and split equally among the four of you. Whatever you kept out of the envelope stays yours.
Highest total after 5 rounds wins. The referee checks every envelope amount and every receipt is a whole number from 0 to 20.

ROUND 1/5. Totals: you 0.0, Ines 0.0, Jo 0.0, Kit 0.0.
Seal your envelope. Reply with [contribute: n], a whole number from 0 to 20.

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
Each contributed token returns only 1.6/4 = 0.4 tokens, so contributing always loses; 0 is dominant regardless of others.
